speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: My Ministerial Statement will address Question Nos 1 to 10 of the Order Paper.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It will also address Question Nos 36, 37, 40, 45 and 46 on the Order Paper for the Sitting yesterday.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: At 5.27 pm, the Braddell Station Manager reported the same on the northbound tracks.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Although the flooded stretch was only between Bishan and Braddell, services had to be suspended on a longer stretch, up to stations with crossover tracks for the trains to turn around.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: By 5.38 pm, SMRT reported that water at the deepest section of track had risen to almost meet the electrified third rail.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The system was designed such that power would have cut off automatically if water levels had risen past the third rail.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Nevertheless, as a safety precaution, SMRT cut off all traction power to the affected tracks at 5.58 pm after all passengers had been safely de-trained to the station platforms, so no commuters were left in the tunnels.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In an unrelated but concurrent incident, train services were suspended in both directions between Marina South Pier and Newton MRT stations from about 5.50 pm, when the same train captain who reported the flooding, spotted electrical arcing at the trackside between Raffles Place and Marina Bay MRT stations.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Electrical arcing occurred because accumulated debris caused a short circuit between an electrified baseplate and a bolt in the ground.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The bolt had been left in place after some renewal works many years ago in 2003.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It should have been removed but it was not.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The short circuit generated sparks and heat, causing the debris to smoulder.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The debris quickly burnt off and the sparks extinguished before the SCDF arrived.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: However, the service suspension was only lifted at 9.22 pm after SMRT had completed the necessary safety checks.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Hence, train services between Ang Mo Kio and Newton remained suspended until the end of scheduled service that day.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Despite assistance from PUB and SCDF, the waters could not be cleared for normal train service to begin the next morning.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The flood waters were only cleared to a safe level at 11.06 am the next day.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: During the service disruptions, free public buses and bridging buses were deployed along the affected stretches.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Announcements on services and alternative transport options were made in stations, on-board trains, on SMRT's and LTA's websites, as well as through mainstream and social media channels.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: While there was inconvenience caused to commuters, safety is our top priority.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The SMRT Operational Control Centre (OCC) staff did the right thing and handled a difficult situation well.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Chief Controller, Mr Tan Kwong Chye, took the decision to detrain the commuters and cut off the traction power to the affected tracks between Bishan and Braddell soon after receiving the first reports of flooding.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Train Service Controller, Mr Tan Ming Hui, single-handedly managed both incidents at Bishan and Marina South Pier, ensuring that train services north of Ang Mo Kio continued to run, and train services south of Newton were resumed as quickly as possible by the same evening.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As the flooding incident was much more serious, I will focus on it in my Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It was not due to any inadequacy in the design of flood prevention measures.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Neither was it due to an extraordinary storm.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The primary flood protection measure is the storm water sump pit.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As the name implies, its purpose is to collect storm water.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The water is then pumped out to external drains, thus preventing it from flowing into and flooding the tunnels.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Engineers size the sump pit and pump capacity at each location based on PUB's estimates for potential rainfall, with a huge buffer.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Specifically, the Bishan storm water sump pit has a capacity of over 5,000 cubic metres.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This is roughly the size of two Olympic-sized swimming pools.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This would have filled 13% of the pit's capacity even if all the three pumps were not working.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: A properly maintained storm water sump pit should be clean, free of sludge, silt and debris, and importantly, empty, in anticipation of the next storm so that it can do its job.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It is also not difficult to check if the storm water sump pit is filled up.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Any maintenance crew looking through the grating at the top of the storm water sump pit can easily tell whether the pit is full or not.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Yet, on the day of the incident, the Bishan storm water sump pit must have been quite full, even before the rain started.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As a result, the rain that evening flowed straight into the tunnels, flooding the stretch between the Bishan and Braddell stations.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The anti-flooding system at Bishan has served us well for the last 30 years and is designed with a huge buffer.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: However, the lack of maintenance, including the failure to check that sub-systems were in working condition, has led to this very sad incident.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Singapore Test Services has also independently verified that each of the five float switches controlling the pump system were functional in themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Why these float switches failed to function normally on 7 October is a subject of the on-going LTA investigation.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Such systems need to be maintained quarterly, and maintenance records were signed off and submitted for December last year, March and June this year − three occasions.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: However, these records do not match any corresponding logs for track access and pump activation.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: No track access approvals were issued for preventive maintenance of the Bishan portal sump pumps on these three dates.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Pump logs also showed that the pumps were not activated for these same dates, which were required as part of the maintenance procedures.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The maintenance team in question comprises a manager, an engineering supervisor and four other crew members.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Of these, three have been with SMRT for more than 20 years, including one who was with SMRT for over 28 years.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Of the remaining three, one was with SMRT for a little over a year; the other two for six and eight years.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The engineering supervisor and four other crew members were directly responsible for maintaining pumps and other facilities in 15 stations from Sembawang to Dhoby Ghaut stations, while the manager is responsible for supervising and ensuring that the work was done.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: These six have been suspended and are assisting SMRT's investigation.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: SMRT is in contact with the National Transport Workers' Union (NTWU), and has assured the union that these suspended officers will be accorded due process.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Apart from Bishan, SMRT has also checked the storm water pump systems at four other tunnel portal locations in Redhill, Kembangan, Lavender and Changi.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: SMRT is currently conducting investigations into the relevant teams responsible for these pumps under the Building and Facilities maintenance group.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Each portal sump is managed by a separate team.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: There are altogether five portal sump pits and five different maintenance teams.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This group, the Building and Facilities maintenance group, was headed by Vice President Ng Tek Poo.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The six include Mr Ng Tek Poo's predecessor, a Vice President who oversaw the unit in charge of maintaining the pump systems prior to May 2017, as well as the Chief Engineer, a Deputy Director and three Managers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Apart from the Building and Facilities maintenance group, which makes up one-tenth of the total staff strength of SMRT Trains, SMRT has not found any evidence of falsification or wilful dereliction of duties in the core railway maintenance and engineering groups who are responsible for the maintenance of trains, signalling and communications, tracks and trackside equipment and power.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Nevertheless, SMRT declared an amnesty period for workers to come forward with information on poor work practices.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This amnesty period closed on 3 November and will be followed by a series of audits by SMRT's Readiness Inspection teams.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As regulator, LTA will also separately assess SMRT's findings on the extent of dereliction of duties and falsification of records.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: While investigations by LTA will take a few more weeks to complete, the facts of the 7 October incident are not complicated, and the cause of the incident is clear.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Meanwhile, SMRT and LTA have taken a number of immediate steps.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: First, SMRT has replaced all existing float switches at the Bishan storm water sump pit.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Second, LTA has enhanced the resilience of the anti-flood system by replacing the pumps at Bishan with heavier duty ones capable of handling water with more sediments and installing additional parallel float switches.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Third, a new radar-based sensor system has been added to independently monitor water levels in the storm water sump pit.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Fourth, the sump pump control panel has been relocated away from the tracks, to enable easier manual access to pump operations, if needed, during operating hours.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: For the other portal systems, SMRT has replaced or repaired all the non-serviceable pumps.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The float switches were also replaced as a precaution.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: SMRT will take swift and stern action to root out any improper practices and prevent a recurrence of this incident.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: First, it has reorganised the unit overseeing the maintenance of the flood protection system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Mr Siu is known to be deeply committed and responsible.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I expect him to enforce greater discipline and process controls within this group.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Mr Siu will report directly to SMRT's Chief Maintenance Officer.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Third, it is tightening the flood recovery plans and intends to strengthen coordination with SCDF and PUB through regular exercises.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Additional emergency equipment, such as portable pumps, are also being procured to augment emergency response capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I happened to have a meeting with a few top Metro operators about a week after this incident.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: And amongst the experts was the former Chairman of Taipei Metro.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Taipei Metro has done very well, as I have shared in this House before, in terms of achieving rail reliability.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: They had plenty of problems, too, in the beginning.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This particular gentleman, Prof Tsai, turned around the company.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I got to know him very well and have met him four times in the last two years that I am in MOT.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: At the meeting last week, I asked him for help.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: He remembered many years ago, he came here for help when we were still running the system quite well.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Although he is the former Chairman, he still has huge influence within Taipei Metro.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: He immediately assembled a team of experts and they are coming in next month.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Last but not least, to develop and cultivate a stronger culture of accountability, ownership and open reporting across the whole organisation, SMRT is strengthening internal processes and staff support.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This includes staff rotations and renewal, delayering of reporting chains for tighter management oversight, enhancing the supervision of night works, strengthening training and coaching of supervisors, and aligning the bonuses and incentives of senior supervisors to the performance of their teams and audit results.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I commend the Chairman for taking these steps and for emphasising that it is the responsibility of management to set the right culture of professionalism and excellence.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: If there is poor work culture, the CEO is responsible.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In response to a journalist's query, he referred to a recent Organisational Climate Survey done by Towers Watson which found nine in 10 SMRT employees proud of, and engaged in their work.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: On the remaining one in 10 employees, he elaborated on the need to strengthen the level of accountability by supervisors and the degree of ownership and open reporting by staff.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I look to the SMRT management to set the right tone of professionalism and excellence to complement the audit systems that are being put in place.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: When we speak of "culture", we mean the culture of the whole ─ the values and practices of management, as much as the values and practices of the workers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: At a senior level, we set the tone, we formulate, we share and then we see to it that the culture is what we have formulated.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I am certain of the new SMRT Chairman's determination and sincere efforts to transform the culture of SMRT as a whole.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: He was appointed Chairman just barely three months ago, but I have known him for many years.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: With the support of management and workers across the organisation, I have faith that he will succeed.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Let us help him along, give him the time and space for him to do the transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Since the incident, I have received questions about the different roles that LTA has played.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: For the rail network, LTA has three distinct roles: as a regulator, developer and asset owner.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Although these three roles are separate, they are all geared towards achieving our vision of a well-connected, reliable and efficient rail network.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: First, as regulator, LTA sets the Operating and Maintenance Performance Standards.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It then conducts regular audits of the operators' maintenance regime and on-site inspections to ensure that the standards are complied with.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: To prioritise its resources, LTA adopts a risk-based approach.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It focuses on the most complex areas where failure could have the most severe impact and damage to the rail network and on passenger safety.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: One example is the signalling system which is the central nervous system of our rail network and is made up of countless interconnected sub-systems located along the tracks, inside the trains, as well as in the stations, depots and Operations Control Centre.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: These complex and high-risk systems are where we place the most audit effort and regulatory focus.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The anti-flooding systems are considered less risky ─ much less risky ─ compared to other core railway systems because the constructs are simple, they are easy to maintain and they have ample engineering buffers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: All these were recorded in the minutes of the meeting.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Dr Richard Kwok, who was Executive Vice President and Chief Technology Officer of ST Kinetics, will start work with SMRT next month.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: His team will report directly to SMRT Board's Audit and Risk Committee.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: He will also jointly head, with LTA, the Joint Readiness Inspection team which will report to the LTA and SMRT Joint Board Technical Committee.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The tighter audit system will help to identify any deficiencies, so that they can be addressed early before faults occur.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: No regulatory oversight can fully guard against intentional efforts to hide mistakes and negligence, especially if it is by a group.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Our operator's efforts to create the right organisational culture of professionalism, excellence and discipline are, therefore, important and they complement the audit systems in place.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Second, as the developer, LTA is responsible for ensuring that our transport infrastructure is appropriately designed with the right specifications.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In developing rail lines, LTA undertakes structured engineering reviews and system assurance assessments, including the Failure Mode, Effects and Criticality Analysis mentioned by Dr Tan Wu Meng, to ensure reliability and safety.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In this case, the design and construction of our MRT infrastructure has incorporated ample flood-resistant specifications and redundancies.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This includes station entrances which are built at least one metre above prevailing flood levels, as well as the provision of ample pump capacity and holding tanks in close consultation with PUB.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: These specifications are more stringent than those for other building developments.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: For existing infrastructure, flood barriers have been retrofitted at older MRT station entrances, such as at Tanjong Pagar and Orchard, to protect these underground stations from the risk of flash floods.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: LTA also works closely with PUB to review the flood protection requirements from time to time, to take into account the impact of climate change and unforeseen weather events on our built-up environment.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In fact, climate change and all these recent freak storms in Asia worry us and Mr Tan Gee Paw, whom I asked to volunteer to be my advisor on rail reliability.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Some four months ago, he wrote me a long email, because there were floods in China, Vietnam and India.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: He is worried that our specifications might not be adequate in this time of climate change and deteriorating weather.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: That was when he got LTA to start reviewing our anti-flood systems.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: And we were just in the midst of the review, including looking at existing systems when, unfortunately, this thing happened.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Third, when the North-South and East-West Lines transitioned to the New Rail Financing Framework in October last year, LTA took over the ownership of all rail operating assets and became an asset owner.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As part of the asset transfer, LTA will assess the condition of the assets while Ernst & Young was engaged to perform due diligence on their Net Book Value.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Payment to SMRT is contingent on the requirement that the condition of the operating assets should befit their age.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Members can then appreciate the extent of assets that we are taking over and that we have to manage and operate.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: LTA has prioritised the condition assessment of critical or high-value operating assets, such as the trains and signalling system first, with the rest, including the Bishan storm water sump pumps, slated to commence later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Of course, we have a payment schedule, we would not pay until we have assessed and it is confirmed by Ernst & Young.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: There is also a fourth and unspoken role for LTA, which I have emphasised since I joined the Ministry two years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: That is, to cultivate a relationship between LTA and the rail operators founded on trust and constructive collaboration towards a common mission of providing reliable rail transport as an essential public service.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I started this because, when I took over, I did a lot of visits above ground, underground, day time, night time.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I was unhappy with the state of adversarial relationship between the regulator and the regulatee.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I told myself, you cannot achieve rail excellence this way.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We may be coming from different entities but, unless you think as one team, one team Singapore, there is no way you can achieve rail excellence, because with that kind of toxic relationship, every time any incident appears, it is finger-pointing. "Not my fault, it is your fault" and he or she says, "not my fault, it is your fault." Then, no way can we solve this problem.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I do not care where you come from, who is your employer, where you get your salary from.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: When a problem crops up, it affects our patients, our customers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Look at it from the customer's point of view, get to the root of the problem and then we settle later who is culpable, who should pay for this, who should pay for that.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: But service recovery first and, more importantly, learn the lesson so that we can prevent future occurrences.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This is especially important now, when our two oldest MRT lines are undergoing major renewal.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: There needs to be a relationship of trust at all levels so that information and ideas are openly, candidly and freely shared and exchanged.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In fact, this helps LTA perform its role as a regulator more effectively as its investigations into any disruptions must always be fair-minded and thorough − having considered all factors like the age of the assets, the effects of weather, design and other extenuating circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Penalties will be imposed if they are warranted, but, at the same time, they must be calibrated reasonably to ensure fairness and accountability.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Such a regulator-regulatee relationship engenders both respect and trust and is critical in our journey towards higher rail reliability.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I have done a lot in the last two years.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I have aged five years along the way.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It is now very different from two years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Looking beyond the North-South Line flooding incident, we remain focused on our larger mission to raise train reliability and to meet the high standards demanded by our commuters.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This is a multi-year effort, involving many critical elements, including replacing ageing assets, investing in engineering skills and manpower, as well as exploiting technology for more effective maintenance.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In the past two years, we have strengthened scheduled maintenance based on the criticality, usage and age of the systems.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We have also begun to go beyond preventive maintenance to predictive maintenance.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Working with LTA, the rail operators will be using real-time condition monitoring and data analytics to track maintenance logs, detect and rectify potential faults before they occur.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This is the next major leap in our efforts to improve rail reliability.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As I have told this House before, our maintenance ramp-up in the last two years is producing results.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: For years, it could not even reach 100,000 train-kilometres.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We were struggling, five digits, cannot even achieve six digits.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: That is how far we have come in the two years.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: But I know the commuters, especially those using the North-South Line regularly, do not feel so.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The MKBF improvements are not what they felt they had experienced.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: And I understand why, because we do have problems with the changing of the signalling system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In other words, as I have explained in this House, we are doing two major assignments: one, improve the rail reliability of existing systems and, two, we are doing projects.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: All metros hate changing signalling systems because, in this modern day of social media, you will get flamed because problems are bound to crop up.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: That is why we pay particular attention to make sure that when we do re-signalling, we test and test and test again, without passengers, that means, during the early hours of the day, so that the bugs can all be identified and debugged and new software patches put in before we launch passenger service.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: If you compare it with the experience of London Underground, for our re-signalling project, we are doing very well, although, as I have said, commuters do not understand it.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: All they know is, every few days, there are some delays here and there.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: So, when I said we are doing well for re-signalling, what I have in mind is versus the experience of the other metros doing re-signalling.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Actually, the problems are being resolved one by one.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Not too long ago, you may remember we had people jumping from platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We put a stop to that with platform screens.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We used to have all kinds of third rail problems; now, no more, because we changed it out.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We had lots of sleeper related problems; now much, much less, as we have also changed it out.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The signalling system has to be changed and we have turned the corner for the North-South Line.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The same is with flooding, it will not recur.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As we keep going in this direction, there will be a major improvement in experience in the near future.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I can only seek commuters' patience and understanding.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: If it were so easy, it would have been fixed years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I do not have to be in MOT.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In the short term, this may cause disruption to commuters, such as during the implementation of re-signalling on the North-South Line.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: When these asset renewal works are progressively completed and as new rail lines open, they will translate into significant improvements in the resilience of our rail network and commuter experience.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This is despite many challenges, the major one being the limited engineering hours available to us to do so many things each day.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Rail operators, and especially SMRT, have to perform both scheduled and corrective maintenance work, and also the implementation of numerous asset renewal works, such as the re-signalling, within the few hours every night when trains are not running.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The punishing schedule takes its toll on the workers and forces operators to prioritise between many urgent and important tasks.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: So far, we have only been able to shorten train operating hours marginally, for example, on some Sundays, to provide more time for the operators to do their job.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Metros elsewhere have the option to close down an entire line for a substantial period.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Closing a major rail line like the North-South and East-West Lines to expedite these renewal works would certainly help us get to our destination sooner.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We just got to do it as quickly as we can.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It is a little bit like what my cardiologist advised me almost eight years ago, when he tested my calcium score and it ran out of the optimal range.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: He told me, "I think you have a serious problem.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: You better do a bypass." I was in denial and said, "I live such a disciplined life.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: How could it happen to me?" And he said, "No, until you fix this one, you are at risk of anytime falling dead." As I was saying, we need to speed up the renewal of ageing assets.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The limited engineering hours are a significant obstacle to achieving this.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I have asked LTA to work with SMRT to see how we can squeeze out more engineering hours for the team.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: For the re-sleepering project, we shortened operating hours on Sundays but only marginally.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Given the scale of outstanding asset replacement programmes, we will need many more extended engineering hours, perhaps even on weekdays.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I seek commuters' understanding and patience should we decide to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I hope to get Members' support for such a programme, especially residents living in the North, like Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and myself.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In summary, the 7 October incident should not have happened.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The SMRT team responsible for maintaining the Bishan storm water sump pit had neglected their duties, falsified records and failed us.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: SMRT management has accepted full responsibility over this sad episode.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The entire leadership is here, up in the Public Gallery.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We have worked hard to improve train reliability and we have made significant progress.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: That is why I got upset when people make generalisations that things have gotten worse.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Things have gotten worse because you think it has gotten worse because of the re-signalling project − the new project.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: If we are not doing any of those new projects, the improvement would have been visible and palpable.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I have interacted with many SMRT staff working on the signalling system, power, trains and track maintenance.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: They are determined to regain the trust and confidence of our commuters.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I know they are just as upset as me that some of their colleagues in charge of maintaining the tunnel portal sump pits have failed us and pushed us back in this multi-year journey.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I share their disappointment and also embarrassment, deeply.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I have invested so much in this assignment.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: But we are determined to get back on our feet, back to our work and soldier on.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I am confident that the new SMRT Chairman, Mr Seah Moon Ming, will be able to turn around the company and that we can catch up with the best metros in the world in terms of service reliability.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The heavy-lifting has to be done by SMRT.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The resources of LTA and MOT will be there to support them.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: That is why my Permanent Secretary is here, too, as well as the CEO of LTA.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Much of their work can only be done when revenue services stop.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I know because I have seen them, I have talked to them in the middle of the night, in the tunnels, on the tracks, at the depots, in the trenches.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope that the Minister and the Ministry would continue to support our rail workers, especially the maintenance workers, as they have always done.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The union does not condone any action by any worker that would harm fellow workers and commuters or damage the operations of our public transport system.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The union will work with SMRT to ensure that due process is given to any worker who has been found not to have done their work properly.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Three, how does LTA ensure that the rapid transit system operators devote sufficient time, resources and money on preventive maintenance of rail assets owned by LTA, so as prevent the premature degradation of these assets, having regard to its life cycle?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I know because, on the ground, Mr Yong is almost always there.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Whenever I am in a depot or the trenches, I always find him there − very committed, as a union leader, and motivating the staff towards this common goal.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We still have a lot of work to do, especially by SMRT, forging this relationship between employer and the workers.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: My advice to them has always been "work with the unions".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: When I ran hospitals, I worked with the unions closely.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: When you have a good bunch of union leaders, you can achieve so much together.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Conversely, if there is lack of trust, there will be trouble.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why I worry a bit when I first read about this amnesty thing because if you do not manage it well, instead of forging trust, in fact, it can cause a deterioration of relationship.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Yesterday, over coffee, Mr Charles Chong was sharing with us the practice in the aviation sector, which I am familiar with.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Amnesty is not something unique or unusual but what is different in the case of aviation, they do it all the time.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In other words, it is an open system.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: At anytime, employees are allowed to own up and the employer would then look into the situation and decide.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But amnesty does not mean a free pass: if you commit a crime or it is a deliberate act of sabotage, then nobody can help you.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But other than that, if for various reasons, you did something stupid and you reflected, you come forward and own up; the employer can be generous in handling this particular case.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In the case of SMRT, this is a new experience for them.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: All the more, I think, they have to handle it carefully, so that we use this opportunity to build up this strong relationship between employer and employee, and unions will play an important part.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: On Mr Murali's various questions, he had three points?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The first question is: does LTA intend to impose a fit and proper criteria on the senior management of rapid transit system operators?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The second question is whether LTA has identified any serious backlog in maintenance of its rail assets to date and, if so, what action has been taken.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The third question is how LTA ensures that rapid transit system operators devote sufficient time, resources and money on preventive maintenance of rail assets, so as to prevent premature degradation of these assets.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Just now, I talked about the last two years and some of the things that we have accomplished.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We call it New Rail Financing Framework (NRFF), whereby we are now owner of the assets.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We were facing some difficulties in the past with the company, especially because it was a listed company, sometimes, there is disagreement about when to replace an ageing asset.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But now that we have taken over, the decision lies with LTA.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: When I say I want to change, we will change.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Because we are the owner, it is of great concern to us now what is the condition of the assets and we have to make sure that it is properly maintained.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why we are the one; it is LTA who sets the maintenance standards and we will do audits to make sure that it is done.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Another major achievement in the last two years was helping Temasek take back the company, so that it is delisted, it is no longer a listed company, and now, it is a Government-owned company.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In fact, that has always been my preferred model which I am much more familiar with.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Members know my background: I spent many years running hospitals and the Restructured Hospital Framework or scheme is what I always preferred, probably because of my own experience and background.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It has the advantage of commercial discipline but, at the same time, it does not have the other problems of being overly focused on the bottom line with results which may not be totally satisfactory from the rail reliability point of view.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Because it is a fully-owned company of the Government, the Board of Directors, the appointment of senior officers are within our control.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: For a large workforce, 10% is a large number; it is not a small number.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: As the Minister mentioned, the culture and tone are set by management.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: So, by increasing frequency, would other works be compromised?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: During the media conference, SMRT had also mentioned that they will be using technology and CCTV to monitor the sump pump area in future.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: As mentioned, the heavy rainfall would have only filled 30% of the reservoir that day.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: So, increasing the frequency, is that the way forward?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: SMRT management has also accepted full responsibility over this sad episode.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Can the Minister provide some clarity to this statement as well?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Is the training provided for the crew sufficient for them to meet their job duties?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The shortage of engineering hours to do so many things is, however, real.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why, wherever we can, using technology or otherwise, trying to improve the productivity of the maintenance staff is key.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But no matter what we do, I think if we can squeeze out more engineering hours so that the team can do more work, it would be the best approach, going forward.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As to penalty, I think I do not want to comment on it yet.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I did make some comment during the press conference because I was starting from the background of what I related to Members that, two years ago, what I observed was that it was not a conducive working environment between regulator and regulatee.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I am worried that if we continue this or restart this adversarial relationship, I think the war is lost.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have worked so hard to achieve this one team that I really would like to preserve this, going forward, or at least until we can stabilise the whole situation and replace all the old assets.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I am not against imposing penalties or providing incentives for extraordinary performance.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But there is a time to do a certain thing.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But during this transition, I prefer to preserve this one team relationship between regulator and regulatee.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The other various pumps in the other portals, I have spoken about it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: There are five portal storm pits for the North-South, East-West Lines.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why although you heard about many pumps – eight pumps, six pumps – they are not of similar capacity.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: These are very small pumps; the pits were all above ground.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If you have visited − unlikely because this is closed to public − you will find Bishan pit to be very unusual.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is underground and because of the surroundings − the Member of Parliament for Bishan may understand it better − the water just flows all the way down.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why we require this 5,000-cubic-metre capacity.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The other sump pits' capacities are not even 10% that of the Bishan pit.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The cultural thing, I have spoken about, Desmond Kuek mentioned this point.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: He has mentioned it a couple of times before as well as during the recent press conference.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I do not want to put words in his mouth, neither can I speak for him.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, I have quoted what he said during the press conference.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I know he has been working very hard to try to change the work culture.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I do not know whether he made it public: 2011 was the last major disruption and then SMRT Board decided to remove their previous CEO.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: He was not parachuted in or being asked to go and fix this.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As a former Chief of Defence Force, I think his heart is in the right place.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We all felt ashamed by these every-now-and-then disruptions in SMRT.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I am an engineer and I have many engineering friends.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For a long time, we compared ourselves with Hong Kong and we said, "We are far ahead of them as engineers".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But when their MTR is running much better than our MRT, it is terrible.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why when I spoke to Mr Tan Gee Paw, he has no qualms.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Immediately, he said "Yes, I will help you".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: He did say, "I am pretty old" and, of course, he is still chairing PUB.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But he volunteered, came forward to help us because he felt it was important.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why this revelation that this small group of people falsified records − this is not the Singaporean culture!

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We are known positively everywhere we go: China, India, people know us.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We are honest, we deliver what we promise.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And yet, to have a bunch of people seemingly doing very funny things, it is really odd.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think some Members asked for the profile of these few people.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Most of them are Singaporeans, some are not.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think four are Singaporeans, three are foreigners.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: All the racial groups are represented among them.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And that is why they are being investigated.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I am sure there will be future updates by SMRT as they make progress in their investigations and take the necessary due process.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But I can assure the unions that they are working together to make sure that staff will be fairly treated.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: After the Committee of Inquiry's (COI) Report which was released in the aftermath of the two train incidents on 15 and 17 December 2011, a number of recommendations were actually made to SMRT and LTA.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, my first question to the Minister is: was this self-assessment actually carried out?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: There were a number of other recommendations, one of which was to review documentary and record keeping to ensure a higher level of accuracy and reliability.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Specifically, with regard to that recommendation, what did SMRT do which could have actually avoided the issue of falsification even though, I hope, it only involved a small number of staff?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In the aftermath of the COI, of course, there were some operational issues that came up.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think the most tragic was the death of the two SMRT workers.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: We had an anonymous source quoted in The Straits Times who shared that the train wheels were not grounded as per the maintenance regime.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This was revealed only a few days ago.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And, of course, the amnesty announcement by SMRT is likely to uncover a few more lapses.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The other question I have relates to a speech Minister made on 30 May 2016 with regard to infrastructure maintenance.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, can I ask the Minister whether these inspectors could have uncovered some of the lapses that happened post-COI and, more specifically, with regard to the unfortunate flooding incident?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Yes, it was my suggestion and instruction to LTA.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I have a couple of reasons for doing so.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: One was in anticipation of new lines that we would be opening − Downtown Line 3 and the Thomson Line.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I just replied to a Parliamentary Question (PQ).

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Through LTA, we recruited as many as possible, so that some of them can then flow out to work for the operators.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The embedding of LTA engineers with the operators is an on-going process.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Every time I visited them, I have to check first, "Where are you from?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Are you from LTA?" And often, there will be a mixture.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I was happy to see them working as a team, as a group.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But as I explained in my Statement, in the last two years, we have been focusing on the most critical areas, which are the trains, the tracks, the signalling.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That has always been our focus because those are the most complicated and the most important.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The other parts, which are the water treatment and so on, those are "小儿科" or "simple stuff" that anybody can do.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Because we were focusing on this side, this other part let us down.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why I was so disappointed and so angry.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But never mind, it has happened, we will fix it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The follow-up on COI, yes, all those things were done.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I know some Members would choose to ignore it and keep on saying, "We have not improved, we have gotten worse", and quote the glitches with the re-signalling to substantiate their criticism.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But it is not so and that would be extremely unfair to the majority of the SMRT staff who are working their guts out.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That was also part of the reason why I reacted how I reacted during one media event several months ago.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I was unhappy with some of the reporting on the re-signalling problems.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I wanted to explain to the people, to the public, that the re-signalling, yes, has a lot of problems.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: All these were anticipated and, actually, we have done better.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But I can understand from a commuter's point of view, they cannot relate, because they have not experienced the re-signalling problems in London.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, they do not have a base line.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: From their points of view, yesterday there was no re-signalling, there were no problems.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Today, how come every three days, there are some breakdowns, some delays here and there?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: To them, they think that the whole system has broken down, when it is not the case.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: On behalf of the residents in Yishun, I would like to thank everyone, especially staff from SMRT who have been working very hard while keeping our trains running on time, most of the time.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second question is that we are quite worried about the morale of the existing staff.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Once you have audit and you are trying to investigate, the morale of the staff would be affected, but we need them to work hard to keep the trains running.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, how can we help the morale of the existing staff?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And for those who really work hard, are we going to reward them?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Because over the last few days, we only heard about punishment, taking away their bonuses.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I think we need to make sure that the morale of the existing staff is maintained and the pride in their jobs is instilled, instead of more and more audits or instead of "I am trying to catch who are not doing their jobs".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I totally agree with the comments from my favourite Member of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I am clear in my mind all the time.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think I have described in this House two years ago when I took on this job, that this is a multi-year war, we are fighting a multi-year war.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I am quite sure you have read Sun Tsu's "Art of War".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: How do we keep morale high all the time is crucial, because along this multi-year journey, there are bound to be disappointments, some defeats and some losses.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: How we react the day after often determines whether the team is likely to win the war, or it is going to lose.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If each time something disappointing happens and then everybody is onto the troop or the general, or worse, calling for a switch of the general, this is a sure strategy for failure.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We should not be blindly loyal to a particular strategy or a particular team.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So long as they are doing their work conscientiously and the milestones regularly show there are improvements, I think we should lend them our support.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As Members of this House, you are influential, you determine how you can help influence your residents' perception, particularly for those with residents living in the north, how they respond to each disruption.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The more we can help to explain to them about the difficulty of the re-signalling system and explain to them that, yes, akan datang, that better days are coming.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And, indeed, in the case of the North-South Line, better days are coming.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Unfortunately, I will soon have to start re-signalling the East-West Line, so Members of Parliament who serve along that corridor, I will need to brief you slowly and carefully, but hopefully, the experience with the North-South Line will help us shorten the learning curve for the East-West Line.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As to pride in staff, that is always crucial.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think I have said in this House several times before, in my previous portfolio.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The Japanese people take pride in their work, even simple work.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They may be rank-and-file, but because they take pride, they own the outcome of their jobs.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, the standard that they deliver is quite different.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I have talked to some metro operators in Japan.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They are finding the new generation not quite the same as the old generation.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But in absolute terms, they are still much better than our people.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Minister responded to my Parliamentary Question (PQ) that we are not holding a COI.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My question relates then to the Audit Committee that is being formed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Does the Ministry plan to bring in international experts to augment the team, to put in best practices, for example, that we can learn from?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: At the same time, to what extent does the Ministry plan to supervise this audit, in terms of how wide, how deep it has to go?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The second question relates to the technologies being used for the pumps.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I understand that some of these are 30 years old, but would the designs be reviewed and relooked, because if we look at the sensors today, we do not need people to monitor that the sump pits are full, for example?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I thought I had mentioned some radar-based sensors that they have already put into the Bishan sump pit to help improve on the system.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As for COI, I have explained why I made the judgement call that there is no need for a COI because this is not a complicated puzzle.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The intention is to make public once the investigations are complete so that the public will get to know what happened, what are the causes and how we are fixing them.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As for international experts, I thought I had mentioned it in the Statement that I have invited this Taipei team to come and have a deep dive into our system to see whether there are new things that we can learn from them.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is stated that staff who come forward would not be penalised.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, does that mean that they will get the same bonus as those staff who were diligently doing their job because this seems to run counter to the principle of fairness and accountability?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The other question I would like to ask the Minister is: is it possible to build more what they call cross-over tracks so that if there is a problem at any point along the track, the train can turn around and we can isolate the fault and we build up the system's resilience?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The Member Mr Charles Chong told me that, in the aviation industry, it is quite well developed.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Whereas when you talk about bonus, a bonus is to reward good performance.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have engineering hours of three hours and we are already complaining that we do not have enough time.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: How do they do maintenance with service going 24 hours?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Even though it was designed 100 years ago − probably that time, land was cheap − they catered for a lot of side tracks and alternative routes so that trains can move to other tracks.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why they were able to continue running 24 hours.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is how a well-designed network ought to be like.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Unfortunately, we do not have this luxury, I think, mainly because we just do not have the land.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I am going to give a speech in a few weeks' time talking about "a tale of two lines", that is, the North-South Line and the new line which we are building, to show how much differences there were during these 30 years.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Remember the Government took a long time to debate, "Should we or should we not build MRT?" That is why when LTA designed the North-South and East-West Lines, they really cut cost.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Members know the North-South Line is a very heavily-used line.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The East-West Line is another very heavily-used line.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And, yet, for a long time, for 30 years, they were relying on just one depot − the Bishan Depot.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Any other line you go and visit, whether it is in Tokyo, London, Taipei, a line like this, sometimes would have two depots or one-and-a-half depots.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And for two lines, there should have been three or four depots.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But I suppose because of budget constraints, we did not have that luxury.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Unless you close down the lines for a longer period.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I am not giving excuses for our team.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But I hope Singaporeans appreciate that it was a very different era when we started.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: You just look at the new lines − Downtown Line 3, for example − the number of exits per station, whereas the North-South and East-West Lines, with one or, at most, two.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And the Hokkiens will say, "Even one, and you will celebrate!"

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Many of our lines are quite skeletal, we do not have alternative or parallel loops.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For the LRT, it is possible to think about it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For the MRT, the capacity difference is just too wide.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For the LRT, in fact, a few weeks ago, I had asked LTA to take a good look at it, especially during off-peaks.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think we should seriously consider shortening the operating hours for LRT and use buses to take care of that.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That will then allow a regular fleet of buses and drivers who may come in useful during peak periods should you have a disruption.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, LRT, I think, possible, and we are thinking along that line.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For MRT, the capacity difference is just too wide.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Even if we have the money to get all the buses and, if we can get all the drivers, the roads will be "choc-a-bloc".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It has no competition on the lines it operates, like the North-South or the East-West Lines.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Corporate energy should be focused on operational reliability.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The second point is this: SMRT is able to apply to LTA for asset replacement grants for eligible operating assets like trains.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, that gives SMRT even more incentive to use its own revenue for maintenance.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Yet, we see maintenance and serious maintenance lapses.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The third point is this: SMRT has a secure customer base.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It provides an essential service − public transport.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It does not have to advertise "Please take my train instead of my competitors'" because SMRT has operational monopoly over the lines it operates.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, SMRT has line monopoly, taxpayer subsidies and a secure customer base.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Where a corporate institution provides an essential service, we cannot tolerate corporate complacency.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, going forward, I have three suggestions for SMRT and I hope MOT will consider these.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: First, revamp the fine model for regulating rail transport operators.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, we should move away, in my humble view, from a mere fine model.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Every 500 hours without injury is a milestone.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Every 10,000 kilometres without a breakdown is a milestone.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Third, SMRT must be proactive rather than reactive.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What does the amnesty tell us or tell me about SMRT?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Is it that the top or middle management does not know what is going on in the tunnels or on the tracks?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, my third question is: how is SMRT going to be proactive rather than reactive in troubleshooting?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think the key is the quality of the leadership.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Two years ago, when the Prime Minister asked me to take on this job, I spent the first couple of weeks meeting a lot of people.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Among the first few people I met was Mr Lim Boon Heng.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: He was, and still is, the Chairman of Temasek, and we had a very long chat.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: At our level, specifically, we were talking about chairmanship, that is, chairmanship of SMRT.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I was quite clear in my suggestion to him that I think because the former chairman had been there for years, it was time for a change.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: He took the point and said he had to start hunting.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If this change in leadership had been executed earlier, maybe we could have avoided this.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The Member's comments about SMRT's monopoly and not focusing on the right priority, I think were probably correct for the previous team.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I have worked with this current team for two years now.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: There are a lot of imperfections, but I think they believe in the cause.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, it is not as if they are distracted, that "I am a monopoly, I could not care less and, therefore, I just do as I wish and then you take it or leave it, customer".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As I have said just now, let us give Mr Seah time and space for him to turn it around.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: He has turned around organisations before and I am confident he can do it.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, I note that the Minister had mentioned that there was some form of prioritising in respect of the audit by LTA on the different aspects.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, I think the Minister mentioned that they were focusing more on the bigger rail reliability issues.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would the Minister agree with me that this was, actually, a grave oversight because the smallest of component can cause a train disruption, and a train disruption is a train disruption.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It could be caused by a defective door or by a bigger component, a bigger fault in the whole system.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think the Minister also mentioned, and I agree, the comparison with the aerospace industry.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I agree with the Minister because in the aerospace industry, the air worthiness certification is required for even the smallest of components for the aircraft.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The point I am trying to say is that, if you cannot get the small things right, you are not going to get the big things right.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, moving forward, will the Minister agree that all audit regimes by LTA – or, in fact, by SMRT, – have to be very thorough?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It has to cover both the small things and the big things.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And, in fact, it was a so-called smaller issue, like the pump.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The cause of the pump failure is actually quite small but if you look at the cause of it, the falsification of the records, the conduct of the whole team, it actually points to an organisational issue.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe my colleague Mr Pritam Singh has also asked about how extensive will the internal audit of SMRT or the review by the Taipei experts be.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Perhaps the Minister can shed more light on how extensive this can be, and can it, for example, be akin to a forensic audit.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Soon after 7 October, I know Mr Seah Moon Ming and I, between the two of us, we probably cumulatively only chalked up 20 hours of sleep.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We just do not have so much time to do so many things.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: When there are so many things to do, we have to set priorities.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, I am not giving excuses for not checking the pumps or other small things the Member talked about.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But in the limited time that we have, we focused on the big ticket items which can cause severe problems.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why we have been focusing our energy on those critical parts.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But we were going to get, eventually, to check on these small things, too.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Unfortunately, the small things cropped up and we got eggs on our face.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And, if needed, we can bring in some of our metro friends from other cities to help us as well.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Thirdly, I would like to clarify with the Minister, what are the main learning points for the project of re-signalling the North-South Line and how can it apply to the East-West Line in reducing the timeframe of project completion, reducing disruptions and making the commuters happy?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The Prime Minister has just reminded me of the need for the Cross Island Line.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The North-South Line has been a great lesson for us, just as the London Underground experience has been a great lesson for us.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That was why we completely changed the schedule of the timeline of the North-South Line project.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For the East-West Line, because the equipment are similar, we believe that the software patches that were put in for the North-South Line ought to be applicable as well.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But because every line is different as – the French engineer told me, every train is different – they have personalities.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: He told me, "You have four generations of trains: old trains, new trains, some new trains and some, just delivered!" So, that is some of the problems that we are facing.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Please do bear with us but we will try our very best to minimise disruptions.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For our Jalan Besar GRC, we have just had the construction of the new train line ─ the Downtown Line 3.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I think a lot of these projects, the train stations actually are, what I know, engineering feats.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I saw a lot of pride in the work by the teams and I just want to thank you for that.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: A lot of solutions that the Minister has mentioned are to do with technical and operational issues.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I wanted to know if the Minister and the agencies involved have gone deep-diving into any of the HR issues.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Things like, we say very broadly, cultural issues.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But cultures take two to three years to establish and to change.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Or even the compensation, the total compensation packages.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Those are specifics that I think need to be looked into.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I am especially thinking of the 90% of the engaged and good staff that the Minister mentioned in the survey that was done by Towers Watson.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, how do we continue to retain the good staff and to balance the need for accountability, of course, versus the perceived intolerance for mistakes and even blaming should things go wrong?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Because that could lead to a lot of fear at the workplace and, in fact, make the culture even more negative.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The internal HR policies and what changes they need to do, that is for SMRT to follow through.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As the Member spoke, I looked at the SMRT leadership at the Public Gallery and they were nodding their heads.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
