text: At my level, it is more about the whole rail industry, how can we make sure that this rail profession remains attractive, especially to young Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We do a lot of work together with institutions, doing roadshows.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is a hard slog because engineering as a profession, is itself not so attractive.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And specifically to rail, and especially when you read about all these rail breakdowns, why would they want to join the industry?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: At the Civil Service level, we have made a lot of changes.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have to encourage young Singaporeans to realise that there is a lot of scope and opportunities to deal with very exciting projects.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And also to reach out to the females.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Each time when I visit the operators, LTA, I am very happy to find young girls joining the industry.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And some of them are actually challenged by these problems that they regularly hear about SMRT's breakdowns.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And they said, "No, I think I want to make a difference." That kind of passion will translate into very good work practices and pride in their work.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think we can be optimistic that we can tackle this problem and, at the same time, attract Singaporeans to join this sunrise industry.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I, once again, want to thank the Minister, the team at LTA and also the SMRT new chairmanship for their efforts.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: There has been talk about the regulator-operator relationship.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The relationship between the people and how they work together.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I think we also have to think a lot about the relationships within the operator, how people at different levels in an organisation, especially one going through a tough time like this, relate to one another.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, if I may just share a personal view, as part of clarification, I think it would be very important that staff always feel comfortable highlighting problems upwards to management, especially if the problem cannot be solved at their own level, and that management continues to want to know what the problems are, to try and fix them.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Rather than engage in a culture of shaming and blaming, which we know does not work in aviation, neither does it work in healthcare.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: It is what the KPI and checkbox represent, the work that is actually done.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: That, again, is the message in aviation as well as in healthcare.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Lastly, also, in addition to condition monitoring and technology for infrastructure and hardware, also using technology to strengthen the "heartware" and help people.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, just as we use technology today to improve audit of corporate finance or of whether tenders are being awarded appropriately in line with appropriate corporate governance, we see this in the corporate sector, likewise using technology to help HR and help workers look for blind spots in their work processes.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Both of us came from the healthcare sector and we know, healthcare learnt from the aviation sector on how to manage safety, how to recover from each incident and how to inculcate a culture whereby people come forward, especially to discuss near-misses, because those are important.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For trains or the rail industry, these constitute a new work culture that they would have to learn.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Fortunately, there are other players in town who know how to manage those things.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Everywhere I go, whether it is health, when I move to a new hospital, I take a "eat humble pie" approach.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Do not be shy about asking and you will discover that there are so many people most willing to share their experience and expertise with you.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Conversely, if you are arrogant, you think "I am the greatest, I know what to do and so on", then you are doomed for failure.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, at the end of the day, it is still about leadership, it is still about how we share and propagate that kind of culture and encourage feedback from the workers and work closely with them.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In the case of Singapore, work closely with the unions because you will find them extremely helpful and useful to you.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Sitoh Yin Pin and then the Minister can wrap up.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Indeed, I always believe that in every organisation, you must be clear what should be your core competencies, those that you must be able to do very well that distinguish you from your competitors or rivals.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Make sure you identify good chaps, trustworthy companies, vendors and, then, you can outsource to them.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The Minister just now expressed his disappointment that Mr Lim Boon Heng, CEO of Temasek Holdings, took too long to appoint a new Chairman of SMRT.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: He must not forget that the mission of SMRT is to make money for the Government.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: I am of the opinion that the multiple problems of the train services, the core of the problem is money.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The Government wanted to have the cake and eat it, expecting profit from the train operator and, at the same time, also expected efficiency, tip-top maintenance work.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: I note that the Minister was steering the existing framework of the checks and balances between the Ministry, which holds the purse strings, the regulator LTA and the operator, towards one team.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: First, MOT, LTA and SMRT, each has a role to play.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: How does the Minister ensure that each of them can still play the functional role well when they work as a team and become good friends?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The second clarification: hammering everyone to work together to solve the problem now as a team is important but what about instituting the structural system of checks that should be embedded to ensure efficiency, honesty and integrity?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We do not have to use SMRT to make money.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is the same thing with restructured hospitals, which I have a lot more experience with.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The reason we restructured is so that we can exploit the financial discipline of the commercial sector, so that in the process of providing this public service, you can get the best cost effectiveness of the operations achieved.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We could have done it as a Government department but I think the decision was not wrong to put it to a corporatised company, fully-owned by the Government.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They know and the leadership of such a company must know and Mr Seah knows it that this is, for example, an engineering outfit.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: You cannot just anyhow go and spend money – buy this, buy that, gold plate everything – and then, of course, you can have marvellous operations.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, when your team fails you, what do you do?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, those things are important lessons for everyone.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: What happens in SMRT has applications for the others as well.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: How do you achieve one team and yet be clear of the boundary, that there are different roles we play?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I thought I had explained that in my Statement.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If you cannot work as one team, I think there will be trouble, as there were troubles in the past.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why it is so important that they function as one team.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, each time a problem crops up, we settle it as one team.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That does not mean that we blur the boundary and, therefore, forget about individual roles and checks and balances.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Yes, it may sound to the Member as schizophrenic, but we are quite clear in our mind and it can be done.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This has been a difficult challenge but not something that we cannot manage.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: My main takeaway in the last two years is, yes, it has cost us, individually, maybe personal health and maybe family life.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: What we are asking of commuters is "Please bear with us because a 30-year train system is a very challenging one".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I was talking to the Hong Kong MTR operator.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Some of their lines will soon be 30 years old and that is why they are watching what is happening here very carefully because they know, we are all engineers, we know systems will get into trouble.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Of course, if you do not need to worry about bottom line, it is straightforward.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Thirty years' shelf life, but let us change everything at 20 years.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Look at the fares elsewhere being charged in other cities.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: These are some of the trade-offs that we have to make.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I genuinely believe that we have made significant improvements.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The re-signalling is a separate issue but we will overcome that and then I think commuters will be able to experience what the MKBF improvement figures actually show.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the Day.
